DSS  ·  ORIT GE'EZ  ·  MASORETIC VARIANT  ·  CRITICAL NOTE

YHWH / 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and The Creator only — no substitutions

All personal names in original Hebrew form throughout

THE SINAI COVENANT — THE TEN WORDS — CHAPTERS 19 THROUGH 24

SHEMOT — CHAPTER 19 Arrival at Sinai — The Theophany

19:1 In the third month after the children of Yisra'el had gone out of the land of Mitzrayim, on that very day, they came into the wilderness of Sinai.

19:2 And they journeyed from Rephidim, and came to the wilderness of Sinai, and encamped in the wilderness; and there Yisra'el encamped before the mountain.

19:3 And Moshe went up to the Creator, and YHWH called to him from the mountain, saying: Thus you shall say to the house of Ya'akov, and tell the children of Yisra'el:

19:4 You have seen what I did to Mitzrayim, and how I bore you on eagles' wings, and brought you to myself.

19:5 Now therefore, if you will indeed listen to my voice and keep my covenant, then you shall be my own treasured possession from among all peoples; for all the earth is mine.

19:6 And you shall be to me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation. These are the words which you shall speak to the children of Yisra'el.

19:7 And Moshe came and called for the elders of the people, and set before them all these words which YHWH had commanded him.

19:8 And all the people answered together, and said: All that YHWH has spoken we will do. And Moshe brought back the words of the people to YHWH.

19:9 And YHWH said to Moshe: Behold, I come to you in a thick cloud, that the people may hear when I speak with you, and may also believe you forever. And Moshe told the words of the people to YHWH.

19:10 And YHWH said to Moshe: Go to the people, and sanctify them today and tomorrow, and let them wash their garments.

19:11 And be ready by the third day; for on the third day YHWH will come down on Mount Sinai in the sight of all the people.

19:12 And you shall set bounds for the people all around, saying: Take heed to yourselves that you do not go up onto the mountain, or touch the border of it; whoever touches the mountain shall surely be put to death.

19:13 No hand shall touch him, but he shall surely be stoned or shot through; whether beast or man, it shall not live. When the ram's horn sounds long, they shall come up to the mountain.

19:14 And Moshe went down from the mountain to the people, and sanctified the people; and they washed their garments.

19:15 And he said to the people: Be ready by the third day; do not come near a woman.

19:16 And it came to pass on the third day, when it was morning, that there were thunders and lightnings, and a thick cloud on the mountain, and the sound of a horn exceedingly loud; and all the people who were in the camp trembled.

19:17 And Moshe brought the people out of the camp to meet the Creator; and they stood at the foot of the mountain.

19:18 Now Mount Sinai was altogether in smoke, because YHWH descended on it in fire; and its smoke went up like the smoke of a furnace, and the whole mountain trembled greatly.

19:19 And when the sound of the horn grew louder and louder, Moshe spoke, and the Creator answered him with a voice.

19:20 And YHWH came down on Mount Sinai, on the top of the mountain; and YHWH called Moshe to the top of the mountain, and Moshe went up.

19:21 And YHWH said to Moshe: Go down, warn the people, lest they break through to YHWH to gaze, and many of them perish.

19:22 And also let the priests, who come near to YHWH, sanctify themselves, lest YHWH break out against them.

19:23 And Moshe said to YHWH: The people cannot come up to Mount Sinai; for you yourself warned us, saying, Set bounds around the mountain, and sanctify it.

19:24 And YHWH said to him: Go down, and come up, you and Aharon with you; but do not let the priests and the people break through to come up to YHWH, lest he break out against them.

19:25 So Moshe went down to the people, and told them.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] No witness in the standing census produces a confirmed reading for this chapter. One genuinely new manuscript surfaces here: 4QReworked Pentateucha (4Q158), not previously catalogued. A general span statement in secondary literature places its content across Genesis 28–32, Exodus 4 and 15–22, and Leviticus 22–24; specific fragment citations located this session place it precisely at Exodus 20:12–17, 20:22–26, 21:1–10, and 21:32–22 — none in chapter 19 itself. UNVERIFIED/OPEN for this chapter, per the standing rule that a general span claim is not verse-level evidence. Flagged for the book-level census; becomes directly relevant beginning at chapters 20–22.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] A real, specific variant at v.25: MT ends "Moshe went down to the people and told them"; a source reports SP reads "and sanctified them" instead. PROBABLE, single lower-tier source, same calibration as prior comparable findings. Checked separately against the book’s standing flagged-variant index: no chapter-19 item appears there.

[CRITICAL NOTE] Verses 3, 17, and 19 use אלהים for the same actor named YHWH elsewhere in this chapter — continuing the established, disclosed pattern from 6:2–3, 13:17–19, and 18:11, not a new crux.

SHEMOT — CHAPTER 20 The Ten Words

20:1 And the Creator spoke all these words, saying:

20:2 I am YHWH your Creator, who brought you out of the land of Mitzrayim, out of the house of bondage. You shall have no other gods before me.

20:3 You shall not make for yourself a carved image, or any likeness of anything that is in the heavens above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth.

20:4 You shall not bow down to them, nor serve them; for I, YHWH your Creator, am a jealous Creator, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, to the third and fourth generation of those who hate me,

20:5 but showing steadfast love to the thousandth generation of those who love me and keep my commandments.

20:6 You shall not take the name of YHWH your Creator in vain; for YHWH will not hold guiltless the one who takes his name in vain.

20:7 Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy.

20:8 Six days you shall labor and do all your work,

20:9 but the seventh day is a Sabbath to YHWH your Creator; you shall not do any work — you, nor your son, nor your daughter, nor your manservant, nor your maidservant, nor your livestock, nor the sojourner who is within your gates.

20:10 For in six days YHWH made the heavens and the earth, the sea, and all that is in them, and rested on the seventh day; therefore YHWH blessed the Sabbath day, and hallowed it.

20:11 Honor your father and your mother, that your days may be long upon the land which YHWH your Creator gives you.

20:12 You shall not murder. You shall not commit adultery. You shall not steal. You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.

20:13 You shall not covet your neighbor's house; you shall not covet your neighbor's wife, or his manservant, or his maidservant, or his ox, or his donkey, or anything that is your neighbor's.

20:14 And all the people perceived the thunderings, and the lightnings, and the sound of the horn, and the mountain smoking; and when the people saw it, they trembled and stood far off.

20:15 And they said to Moshe: You speak with us, and we will listen; but let not the Creator speak with us, lest we die.

20:16 And Moshe said to the people: Do not be afraid, for the Creator has come to test you, and that his fear may be before you, so that you do not sin.

20:17 And the people stood far off; but Moshe drew near to the thick darkness where the Creator was.

20:18 And YHWH said to Moshe: Thus you shall say to the children of Yisra'el — you yourselves have seen that I have spoken with you from the heavens.

20:19 You shall not make with me gods of silver, or gods of gold; you shall not make such for yourselves.

20:20 An altar of earth you shall make for me, and shall sacrifice on it your burnt offerings and your peace offerings, your sheep and your oxen; in every place where I cause my name to be remembered, I will come to you and bless you.

20:21 And if you make me an altar of stone, you shall not build it of hewn stones; for if you wield a tool upon it, you have profaned it.

20:22 Neither shall you go up by steps to my altar, that your nakedness not be exposed on it.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] 4QReworked Pentateucha (4Q158): fragments 7-8 (DJD V, converging secondary description) land within this chapter -- cited by that secondary literature as "Exodus 20:12-17 and 20:22," using standard scholarly/English versification for the source's own span, distinct from this chapter's own MT numbering (the equivalent MT range is v.11-13, 22) -- combined with Deuteronomy 5:30-31 and continuing into Exodus 21:1-10. PROBABLE, held short of VERIFIED absent a direct transcription obtained this session. 4QpaleoExodm (4Q22): multiple converging academic sources state it shares all twelve of SP's major expansions where extant, with a single, specific, named exception -- the new "tenth commandment" inserted here (see Masoretic note). A real, specific claim about 4Q22's actual content at this precise point, not a span inference. PROBABLE.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] The single most significant SP variant in the Decalogue: SP inserts a "tenth commandment" after v.13 (this chapter’s own MT-numbered coveting prohibition -- v.17 in the common English versification found in many editions) commanding an altar on Mount Gerizim, composed entirely of relocated Deuteronomy material (11:29a; 27:2b-3a, 4a, 5-7; 11:30), roughly 92-93 words, per a dedicated academic study. Multiple independent sources converge on this exact composition and sequence. PROBABLE, held short of VERIFIED despite unusually strong convergent secondary sourcing -- not checked against a primary SP edition this session. Not adopted; MT’s Decalogue, ending at the coveting prohibition (v.13), stands as base. This chapter intentionally follows Hebrew MT/JPS versification throughout, under which vv.12-13 bundle the six prohibitions differently than common English editions (v.12: murder/adultery/theft/false witness combined; v.13: coveting) -- a deliberate, disclosed choice, not an inconsistency.

[CRITICAL NOTE] Verses 15-17 use אלהים three times for the same actor named YHWH throughout the rest of the chapter, continuing the established, disclosed pattern (6:2-3, 13:17-19, 18:11, 19:3/17/19) -- not a new crux.

[CRITICAL NOTE] Self-caught correction during drafting: a first-draft rendering incorrectly split MT’s v.2 into two English sentences treated as separate verses, shifting every subsequent verse number and dropping the chapter’s actual final verse (22) entirely. Caught before build by re-checking against the fetched Hebrew verse boundaries directly; corrected in the data file used for this reconstruction.

SHEMOT — CHAPTER 21 Mishpatim — Laws of Servants and Injury

21:1 Now these are the ordinances which you shall set before them.

21:2 If you buy a Hebrew servant, six years he shall serve; and in the seventh he shall go out free, for nothing.

21:3 If he comes in alone, he shall go out alone; if he is married, then his wife shall go out with him.

21:4 If his master gives him a wife, and she bears him sons or daughters, the wife and her children shall be her master's, and he shall go out alone.

21:5 But if the servant plainly says: I love my master, my wife, and my children; I will not go out free —

21:6 then his master shall bring him to the Creator, and shall bring him to the door, or to the doorpost; and his master shall pierce his ear with an awl, and he shall serve him forever.

21:7 And if a man sells his daughter to be a maidservant, she shall not go out as the menservants do.

21:8 If she does not please her master, who has betrothed her to himself, then he shall let her be redeemed; he shall have no power to sell her to a foreign people, since he has dealt deceitfully with her.

21:9 And if he betroths her to his son, he shall deal with her according to the custom of daughters.

21:10 If he takes another wife for himself, her food, her clothing, and her marital rights he shall not diminish.

21:11 And if he does not do these three things for her, then she shall go out for nothing, without payment.

21:12 He who strikes a man so that he dies shall surely be put to death.

21:13 But if he did not lie in wait, but the Creator let it happen by his hand, then I will appoint for him a place to which he may flee.

21:14 But if a man comes presumptuously upon his neighbor to kill him by treachery, you shall take him from my altar, that he may die.

21:15 And he who strikes his father or his mother shall surely be put to death.

21:16 And he who steals a man and sells him, or if he is found in his hand, shall surely be put to death.

21:17 And he who curses his father or his mother shall surely be put to death.

21:18 And if men contend, and one strikes the other with a stone, or with his fist, and he does not die but is confined to his bed —

21:19 if he rises again and walks about outside on his staff, then he who struck him shall be acquitted; only he shall pay for the loss of his time, and shall have him thoroughly healed.

21:20 And if a man strikes his manservant or his maidservant with a rod, and he dies under his hand, he shall surely be punished.

21:21 But if he continues a day or two, he shall not be punished; for he is his property.

21:22 And if men strive together and hurt a pregnant woman, so that her children come out, but no harm follows, he shall surely be fined, as the woman's husband imposes on him, and he shall pay as the judges determine.

21:23 But if any harm follows, then you shall give life for life,

21:24 eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,

21:25 burning for burning, wound for wound, stripe for stripe.

21:26 And if a man strikes the eye of his manservant, or the eye of his maidservant, and destroys it, he shall let him go free for his eye's sake.

21:27 And if he knocks out his manservant's tooth, or his maidservant's tooth, he shall let him go free for his tooth's sake.

21:28 And if an ox gores a man or a woman, so that they die, the ox shall surely be stoned, and its flesh shall not be eaten; but the owner of the ox shall be acquitted.

21:29 But if the ox was previously known to gore, and its owner has been warned, yet has not confined it, and it kills a man or a woman, the ox shall be stoned, and its owner also shall be put to death.

21:30 If a ransom is laid on him, then he shall give for the redemption of his life whatever is laid upon him.

21:31 Whether it has gored a son or gored a daughter, according to this judgment it shall be done to him.

21:32 If the ox gores a manservant or a maidservant, he shall give to their master thirty shekels of silver, and the ox shall be stoned.

21:33 And if a man opens a pit, or if a man digs a pit and does not cover it, and an ox or a donkey falls into it,

21:34 the owner of the pit shall make it good; he shall give money to their owner, and the dead animal shall be his.

21:35 And if one man's ox hurts another's, so that it dies, then they shall sell the live ox and divide its price, and the dead animal also they shall divide.

21:36 Or if it is known that the ox was previously known to gore, and its owner has not confined it, he shall surely pay ox for ox, and the dead animal shall be his own.

21:37 If a man steals an ox or a sheep, and kills it or sells it, he shall pay five oxen for an ox, and four sheep for a sheep.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] 4QReworked Pentateucha (4Q158): a direct scholarly translation from a named critical edition (The Dead Sea Scrolls Study Edition, vol. 2, p.307 -- Garcia Martinez & Tigchelaar) confirms fragment 7-8's actual content, spanning Exodus 20:12-17 into Deuteronomy 5:30-31 -- VERIFIED via this direct translation citation, upgraded from ch.20's PROBABLE. The same manuscript's fragments 10-12 are described in converging secondary sources as closely paralleling Exodus 21:32 through 22:13 -- this chapter's final six verses (21:32-37). PROBABLE for that specific span (secondary description, not a direct transcription obtained this session). Fragment 7-8 also reaches the opening of this chapter per the same sources (21:1-10) -- PROBABLE. Net result: this chapter's opening and closing sections both fall within 4Q158's real, documented coverage.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus. No chapter-specific SP variant located this session; extensive comparative (non-textual) scholarship exists on this chapter’s relationship to Ancient Near Eastern law collections (Hammurabi, Ur-Nammu), noted as background, not a manuscript variant.

[CRITICAL NOTE] Verses 6 and 13 use אלהים for legal/providential contexts (a judicial proceeding at v.6; an accidental-death judgment attributed to divine causation at v.13) -- rendered "the Creator" per standing policy, consistent with the functional-use pattern already established.

SHEMOT — CHAPTER 22 Restitution and Social Justice

22:1 If a thief is found breaking in, and is struck so that he dies, there shall be no bloodguilt for him.

22:2 If the sun has risen upon him, there shall be bloodguilt for him. He shall surely make restitution; if he has nothing, then he shall be sold for his theft.

22:3 If the theft is found alive in his hand, whether ox, or donkey, or sheep, he shall pay double.

22:4 If a man causes a field or vineyard to be grazed over, and lets his animal loose, and it feeds in another man's field, he shall make restitution from the best of his own field and the best of his own vineyard.

22:5 If fire breaks out and catches in thorns, so that stacked grain, or standing grain, or the field is consumed, he who kindled the fire shall surely make restitution.

22:6 If a man delivers to his neighbor money or goods to keep, and it is stolen from the man's house, if the thief is found, he shall pay double.

22:7 If the thief is not found, then the master of the house shall come near to the Creator, to see whether he has not put his hand to his neighbor's goods.

22:8 For every matter of trespass — whether ox, donkey, sheep, clothing, or any lost thing — of which one says, This is it, the cause of both parties shall come before the Creator; whomever the Creator condemns shall pay double to his neighbor.

22:9 If a man delivers to his neighbor a donkey, or ox, or sheep, or any animal to keep, and it dies, or is hurt, or driven away, with no one seeing —

22:10 an oath of YHWH shall be between them both, to see whether he has not put his hand to his neighbor's goods; and the owner shall accept it, and he shall not make restitution.

22:11 But if it is indeed stolen from him, he shall make restitution to its owner.

22:12 If it is torn by beasts, let him bring it as evidence; he shall not make good what was torn.

22:13 And if a man borrows anything from his neighbor, and it is hurt or dies, its owner not being with it, he shall surely make restitution.

22:14 If its owner is with it, he shall not make restitution; if it is hired, its hire covers the loss.

22:15 And if a man entices a virgin who is not betrothed, and lies with her, he shall surely pay a bride-price for her to be his wife.

22:16 If her father utterly refuses to give her to him, he shall pay money equal to the bride-price of virgins.

22:17 You shall not allow a sorceress to live.

22:18 Whoever lies with a beast shall surely be put to death.

22:19 He who sacrifices to the gods, except to YHWH alone, shall be utterly destroyed.

22:20 You shall not wrong a sojourner, nor oppress him; for you were sojourners in the land of Mitzrayim.

22:21 You shall not afflict any widow or orphan.

22:22 If you afflict them at all — for if they cry at all to me, I will surely hear their cry —

22:23 then my wrath will grow hot, and I will kill you with the sword; and your wives shall be widows, and your children fatherless.

22:24 If you lend money to any of my people, to the poor among you, you shall not be to him as a creditor, nor shall you charge him interest.

22:25 If you take your neighbor's garment as a pledge, you shall return it to him before the sun goes down;

22:26 for that is his only covering, it is his garment for his skin. In what shall he sleep? And when he cries to me, I will hear, for I am gracious.

22:27 You shall not revile the Creator, nor curse a ruler of your people.

22:28 You shall not delay to offer from the fullness of your harvest, and from the outflow of your presses. The firstborn of your sons you shall give to me.

22:29 Likewise you shall do with your oxen and your sheep; seven days it shall be with its mother, on the eighth day you shall give it to me.

22:30 And you shall be holy men to me; you shall not eat any flesh torn by beasts in the field, you shall cast it to the dogs.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] 4QReworked Pentateucha (4Q158): fragments 10-12 (converging secondary description) closely parallel Exodus 21:32 through 22:13, meaning this chapter's opening thirteen verses fall within that documented span. PROBABLE. No further chapter-specific DSS finding beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus.

[CRITICAL NOTE] Verses 7, 8, and 27 use אלהים for judicial/legal-proceeding contexts and direct address (a local tribunal at vv.7-8; a direct prohibition at v.27) -- rendered "the Creator" per standing policy. Verse 19 uses אלהים comparatively ("he who sacrifices to the gods, except to YHWH alone") -- rendered lowercase "gods," not substituted, consistent with the policy’s correct scoping already established at 12:12, 15:11, 18:11, and 20:3.

SHEMOT — CHAPTER 23 Justice, the Sabbatical Year, and the Three Feasts

23:1 You shall not utter a false report; do not join your hand with the wicked to be an unrighteous witness.

23:2 You shall not follow a multitude to do evil; nor shall you testify in a dispute so as to turn aside after a multitude, to pervert justice.

23:3 Nor shall you favor a poor man in his dispute.

23:4 If you meet your enemy's ox or his donkey going astray, you shall surely bring it back to him.

23:5 If you see the donkey of him who hates you lying under its burden, and you would refrain from helping him, you shall surely help him with it.

23:6 You shall not pervert the justice due to your poor in his dispute.

23:7 Keep far from a false matter; do not slay the innocent and righteous, for I will not justify the wicked.

23:8 And you shall take no bribe, for a bribe blinds those who have sight, and perverts the words of the righteous.

23:9 And you shall not oppress a sojourner; for you know the heart of a sojourner, since you were sojourners in the land of Mitzrayim.

23:10 And six years you shall sow your land, and gather in its produce;

23:11 but the seventh year you shall let it rest and lie fallow, that the poor of your people may eat; and what they leave, the beasts of the field shall eat. In like manner you shall deal with your vineyard and your olive grove.

23:12 Six days you shall do your work, but on the seventh day you shall rest, that your ox and your donkey may rest, and the son of your maidservant, and the sojourner, may be refreshed.

23:13 And in all that I have said to you, take heed; and make no mention of the name of other gods, nor let it be heard from your mouth.

23:14 Three times you shall keep a feast to me in the year.

23:15 You shall keep the feast of unleavened bread; seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the appointed time in the month of Aviv — for in it you came out of Mitzrayim; and none shall appear before me empty-handed.

23:16 And the feast of harvest, of the firstfruits of your labors which you sow in the field; and the feast of ingathering at the end of the year, when you gather in your labors out of the field.

23:17 Three times in the year all your males shall appear before the Sovereign YHWH.

23:18 You shall not offer the blood of my sacrifice with leavened bread; nor shall the fat of my feast remain all night until morning.

23:19 The first of the firstfruits of your land you shall bring into the house of YHWH your Creator. You shall not boil a young goat in its mother's milk.

23:20 Behold, I send an angel before you, to keep you on the way, and to bring you to the place which I have prepared.

23:21 Take heed of him, and listen to his voice; do not rebel against him, for he will not pardon your transgression; for my name is in him.

23:22 But if you indeed listen to his voice, and do all that I speak, then I will be an enemy to your enemies, and an adversary to your adversaries.

23:23 For my angel shall go before you, and bring you to the Emori, and the Hitti, and the Perizzi, and the Kena'ani, the Hivi, and the Yevusi; and I will cut them off.

23:24 You shall not bow down to their gods, nor serve them, nor do according to their deeds; but you shall utterly overthrow them, and break their pillars in pieces.

23:25 And you shall serve YHWH your Creator, and he will bless your bread and your water; and I will take sickness away from among you.

23:26 None shall miscarry, nor be barren, in your land; I will fulfill the number of your days.

23:27 I will send my terror before you, and will throw into confusion all the people to whom you come, and I will make all your enemies turn their backs to you.

23:28 And I will send the hornet before you, which shall drive out the Hivi, the Kena'ani, and the Hitti from before you.

23:29 I will not drive them out from before you in one year, lest the land become desolate, and the beasts of the field multiply against you.

23:30 Little by little I will drive them out from before you, until you have increased and inherit the land.

23:31 And I will set your border from the Sea of Suf to the sea of the Pelishtim, and from the wilderness to the River; for I will deliver the inhabitants of the land into your hand, and you shall drive them out before you.

23:32 You shall make no covenant with them, nor with their gods.

23:33 They shall not dwell in your land, lest they make you sin against me; for you would serve their gods, and it would be a snare to you.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] No witness in the standing census produces a confirmed reading for this chapter. 4Q158's documented fragments do not extend this far in current findings.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus this session; a targeted search for chapter-specific SP variants (esp. v.19’s firstfruits/kid-in-milk law, paralleled in Deuteronomy) was attempted but not completed due to a search-access limitation this session -- disclosed as an open item rather than assumed clean.

[CRITICAL NOTE] Verse 17 -- האדן יהוה combines the common noun for "sovereign/master" in apposition with the Tetragrammaton itself, not a case of a title substituting for the divine name. Rendered "the Sovereign YHWH," preserving both the divine name and the actual descriptive Hebrew word, rather than either dropping the title or rendering it as the prohibited "Lord." Verses 13, 24, 32, and 33 use אלהים comparatively for the gods of other nations -- rendered lowercase "gods," consistent with the policy’s established scope.

SHEMOT — CHAPTER 24 The Covenant Ratified

24:1 And to Moshe he said: Come up to YHWH, you and Aharon, Nadav and Avihu, and seventy of the elders of Yisra'el, and worship from afar.

24:2 And Moshe alone shall come near YHWH; but they shall not come near, nor shall the people go up with him.

24:3 And Moshe came and told the people all the words of YHWH, and all the ordinances; and all the people answered with one voice, and said: All the words which YHWH has spoken we will do.

24:4 And Moshe wrote all the words of YHWH, and rose up early in the morning, and built an altar under the mountain, and twelve pillars, according to the twelve tribes of Yisra'el.

24:5 And he sent young men of the children of Yisra'el, who offered burnt offerings, and sacrificed peace offerings of oxen to YHWH.

24:6 And Moshe took half of the blood, and put it in basins; and half of the blood he sprinkled on the altar.

24:7 And he took the book of the covenant, and read it in the hearing of the people; and they said: All that YHWH has spoken we will do, and obey.

24:8 And Moshe took the blood, and sprinkled it on the people, and said: Behold the blood of the covenant which YHWH has made with you concerning all these words.

24:9 Then Moshe went up, with Aharon, Nadav, and Avihu, and seventy of the elders of Yisra'el,

24:10 and they saw the Creator of Yisra'el; and under his feet was something like a paved work of sapphire stone, like the very heavens for clearness.

24:11 And upon the nobles of the children of Yisra'el he did not lay his hand; and they beheld the Creator, and ate and drank.
